s3.title: Amazon S3
s3.summary: Vyomi serves the S3 REST API from its own S3 engine (core/s3_object_core.py) and, on the offline appliance, also writes object bytes through to a MinIO container.
wire: boto3 / aws-cli / AWS SDK v2 / SDK v3 with only the endpoint changed

offline.notes: Buckets, versions, ACLs, policies and all sub-resources live in the appliance's space-scoped state (SQLite) and are served by the same core Nano uses. Object bytes are also written to MinIO so external S3 tools can read them; the mirror is best-effort and skipped (logged once) when MinIO is unreachable, in which case the inline bytes in state still serve S3.

nano.notes: The same core runs in the browser tab over an in-memory object store that is snapshotted to IndexedDB. External SDKs reach it only through the Vyomi relay or the local vyomi-tunnel while the tab is open; there is no MinIO and no on-disk bucket. Browser memory and storage limits apply (not measured here).

differs: Requests are not authenticated: SigV4 is read for routing but never verified, and bucket policies/ACLs are stored but not evaluated for authorization.
Default encryption headers (x-amz-server-side-encryption, KMS key id) are returned, but objects are not encrypted at rest.
Lifecycle, Intelligent-Tiering and Inventory run lazily on read/list rather than on a background schedule.
Replication is synchronous and stays inside the simulator account.
Public Access Block and Object Ownership are enforced only for new ACL/policy writes; existing grants are not retroactively revoked.
Static website hosting, Transfer Acceleration and Requester Pays are wire-level emulations on Vyomi's own host (no real website/accelerate endpoints, no billing payer).
Storage Lens, Access Analyzer for S3, Marketplace for S3 and metadata tables are computed from the simulator's own contents and catalog, not from AWS telemetry.
notInScope: S3 durability and multi-AZ replication of stored data
AWS billing, request-payer charges and S3 storage-class pricing
Real S3 Express One Zone latency and zonal placement
Real website, CloudFront or Transfer Acceleration edge endpoints

s3tables.title: Amazon S3 Tables
s3tables.summary: S3 Tables control plane implemented in Vyomi's own core over the same object store.

offline.notes: Table buckets, namespaces and table metadata are records in appliance state; no Iceberg query engine is attached (not verified beyond the registry text).

nano.notes: Same core in the browser tab.

differs: See the s3.account.table-buckets entry in core/capabilities/aws/s3.json for the exact supported operations and limits.

s3vectors.title: Amazon S3 Vectors
s3vectors.summary: S3 Vectors API implemented in Vyomi's own core.

offline.notes: Vector buckets, indexes and vectors held in appliance state.

nano.notes: Same core in the browser tab.

differs: See the s3.account.vector-buckets entry in core/capabilities/aws/s3.json for exact limits (search is computed by Vyomi, not by AWS's index).

dynamodb.title: Amazon DynamoDB
dynamodb.summary: Vyomi runs its own DynamoDB engine (core/dynamodb_core.py) on both substrates; DynamoDB Local is used only for a one-time migration of pre-v4 data.
wire: boto3 / aws-cli / SDK v2 / SDK v3 with only the endpoint changed

offline.notes: Tables and typed items live in the appliance's space-scoped state, so the console and the SDK see the same data. The amazon/dynamodb-local container in the compose files is only read once to copy tables from a pre-v4 install (VYOMI_DDB_MIGRATE_FROM_LOCAL=0 disables it); it is not on the request path.

nano.notes: Same core in the tab over an in-memory store snapshotted to IndexedDB. External SDKs need the relay or vyomi-tunnel with the tab open.

differs: Per the registry, tables smaller than 3 characters are accepted and a CreateTable without billing mode creates an on-demand table (AWS requires provisioned throughput).
New tables and indexes are ACTIVE immediately.
Scan returns items in key order, not hash order, so page and segment boundaries differ from AWS.
The 1 MB page limit is not applied to Query/Scan and Batch operations never return unprocessed items.
TTL deletes happen when items are read, not by a background sweep.
Point-in-time restore and exports always use the current table state; there is no change history.
Streams use one shard that never splits and keep at most 1000 records.
Encryption at rest and table class are stored but have no effect.
Differential tests against DynamoDB Local pass 149 of 152 hand-written cases (per registry); the 3 deviations are TTL and CreateTable related.
notInScope: Partitioning, adaptive capacity and multi-AZ replication
Real cross-Region global table replication endpoints
DAX binary wire protocol (cache engine is reachable only through Vyomi hooks)

dax.title: Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX)
dax.summary: A real read/write-through cache engine in Vyomi's own core in front of the DynamoDB store, reachable through the DAX management API only.

offline.notes: Cluster records persist in appliance state; the item/query cache is per process and lost on restart.

nano.notes: Same core in the tab.

differs: The DAX client binary protocol is not exposed, so the cache is reachable only through Vyomi conformance hooks.
A rebooted node drops the whole cluster cache.
notInScope: DAX node hardware and cluster discovery endpoint

sqs.title: Amazon SQS
sqs.summary: Vyomi implements SQS in its own core (core/sqs_core.py) with timestamp-based visibility, FIFO, dead-letter queues and both the JSON and legacy Query wire protocols.
wire: SQS Query protocol + XML (older SDKs, curl)

offline.notes: Queues and messages persist in the space-scoped state shared with SNS and EventBridge, so fan-out into queues is a real receivable message. ElasticMQ and NATS exist in the compose files, but the default v4 wire does not use them (ElasticMQ queues are only adopted once on upgrade).

nano.notes: Same core and message semantics in the tab. There is no durable background worker, so delivery to other services happens synchronously inside API calls while the tab is open.

differs: Message redrive tasks complete immediately and report COMPLETED; there is no RUNNING task to cancel.
Lambda event-source mappings invoke synchronously, one message per invocation, the instant SendMessage returns; BatchSize and batching window are stored but ignored.
EventBridge Pipes forward the raw message body instantly; enrichment and input templates are not applied.
SQS metrics are published to Vyomi's CloudWatch from real queue activity as it happens.
notInScope: Multi-AZ durability and AWS throughput limits
Server-side encryption with real KMS data keys (attribute is stored)

sns.title: Amazon SNS
sns.summary: Vyomi implements SNS in its own core (core/sns_core.py) on the native Query/XML wire with real fan-out into SQS queues sharing the same messaging store.
wire: boto3 / aws-cli / SDKs with only the endpoint changed

offline.notes: SQS subscriptions receive a real SNS envelope message. HTTP/S, Lambda and email deliveries are sent by the appliance's delivery worker with the configured retry policy (per the registry).

nano.notes: SQS fan-out works. There is no durable delivery worker, so HTTP/S, Lambda and email deliveries are only recorded in the delivery log, not sent.

differs: Topic access policies are stored but never evaluated.
SMS and mobile push are never delivered; messages go to a simulated handset/device inbox readable through Vyomi-only actions.
Server-side encryption (KmsMasterKeyId) round-trips but message bodies are not encrypted.
Data protection policies use a regex subset of managed identifiers (email, card, SSN, IP).
VyomiMaximumMessageSize is a Vyomi extension attribute.
notInScope: Real SMS carriers and APNS/FCM/ADM push gateways
AWS billing and SMS spend accounting beyond a flat estimate

kms.title: AWS Key Management Service
kms.summary: Vyomi implements KMS in its own core (core/kms_core.py) with software key material stored in appliance state (no HSM).
wire: boto3 / aws-cli / SDKs with only the endpoint changed

offline.notes: Keys, aliases and material are space-scoped state. Pre-v4 Vault-backed keys are adopted once and old vault:v1 ciphertext still decrypts; Vault is not used for new keys.

nano.notes: Same core and key store in the tab; key material lives in browser memory and the IndexedDB snapshot.

differs: Key policies are stored but never evaluated.
Sign/Verify, MAC and ML-KEM use Vyomi's own authenticated primitive, not real RSA/ECC/ML-DSA/ML-KEM math, so signatures only verify inside Vyomi.
Rotation fires lazily on the next operation, not on a clock.
CloudHSM and external key stores are backed by a software HSM stand-in (cluster-vyomisofthsm).
notInScope: Key material export guarantees and AWS-side key durability
Real external key store proxies or CloudHSM clusters

secretsmanager.title: AWS Secrets Manager
secretsmanager.summary: Vyomi implements Secrets Manager in its own core (core/secrets_core.py), encrypting values with its KMS core when a customer key is set.
wire: boto3 / aws-cli / SDKs with only the endpoint changed

offline.notes: Secrets and every version live in space-scoped state. Pre-v4 Vault KV secrets are adopted once; Vault is not on the request path for new secrets.

nano.notes: Same core in the tab.

differs: Resource policies are validated and guarded against public access but not used to authorize calls.
Rotation schedules fire lazily on the next read, not on a clock.
Rotation through a Lambda function is real (four-step protocol) but only for Python functions Vyomi can run.
Cross-Region replication reads the owner's live version; replicas have no independent regional endpoint.
DocumentDB has no backing service, so its picker is unavailable.
notInScope: Real cross-Region replication latency and durability
AWS-managed rotation Lambda templates for third-party databases

iam.title: AWS Identity and Access Management
iam.summary: Vyomi implements IAM management and policy evaluation in its own core (core/iam_core.py), but does not enforce IAM policies on other services' API calls.
wire: boto3 / aws-cli / Terraform with only the endpoint changed

offline.notes: Users, groups, roles, policies, access keys and MFA devices persist in space-scoped state; pre-v4 records are adopted once.

nano.notes: Same core in the tab.

differs: IAM policies are stored and evaluated by SimulatePrincipalPolicy and the policy simulator, but a call an IAM policy would deny still succeeds against S3, DynamoDB and other services.
Service control policies are stored and can be evaluated, but every principal is in the management account so they restrict nothing.
Only virtual MFA (TOTP) is modeled; hardware keys and passkeys are not.
Last-accessed data covers only requests signed with an IAM user's own access key.
Certificates and SSH keys are format-checked, never cryptographically verified.
STS does not mint region-scoped tokens and AssumeRole is not modeled (per registry).
notInScope: Real cross-account trust and multiple member accounts

organizations.title: AWS Organizations
organizations.summary: Management-account control plane in Vyomi's own core inside a single-account simulator.

offline.notes: Organization, OUs, accounts, handshakes and policies are records; member accounts have no resources of their own.

nano.notes: Same core in the tab.

differs: CreateAccount completes immediately.
SCP/RCP documents are validated and evaluable but restrict nothing.
notInScope: Real member accounts, consolidated billing, cross-account access

rds.title: Amazon RDS
rds.summary: Vyomi implements the RDS control plane in its own core (core/rds_core.py) and runs SQL on an embedded engine (SQLite offline, PGlite or SQLite in the browser) reachable through the RDS Data API.
wire: boto3 / aws-cli / Terraform with only the endpoint changed

tech: SQLite (one file per DB instance per space)
offline.notes: Each DB instance's rows live in a SQLite file under the appliance state directory. The compose stack also ships postgres:16 and mysql:8 containers from the pre-v4 handler, but the v4 RDS store does not connect to them; whether any other route still uses them is not verified.

tech: PGlite (Postgres compiled to WASM, loaded from a CDN)
nano.notes: Postgres-family instances use PGlite when it loads, otherwise sqlite3; MySQL/MariaDB instances run on sqlite with MySQL SQL translated. A Postgres/MySQL wire port is bridged to the tab only through the local vyomi-tunnel (core/db_endpoints.py); not exercised here.

differs: The engine is SQLite (offline) or PGlite/SQLite (Nano), not a Postgres or MySQL server, so engine-specific behaviour, extensions and performance differ.
The registry states the Postgres/MySQL TCP wire is not exposed, so an unmodified psycopg2/mysqlclient connection cannot reach an offline instance; use the Data API or query editor.
Data API transactions are real and hold a connection open; max_connections is enforced against them.
Parameter groups, option groups and subnet groups are stored without engine-level effect.
RDS Proxy is a record; connections are not proxied.
Metrics and logs cover only what Vyomi actually observes (Data API activity and statement errors).
notInScope: Multi-AZ storage replication and automated failover hardware
Aurora storage layer and RDS Custom hosts
Engine process logs such as slow-query and checkpoint logs

dms.title: AWS Database Migration Service
dms.summary: DMS control plane in Vyomi's own core migrating between simulator databases with a 'CDC-lite' re-read model.

offline.notes: Reads and writes rows through the simulator's SQL engine.

nano.notes: Same core in the tab.

differs: CDC re-reads the source when a task is described/reloaded; there is no WAL or binlog reader.
Transformation rules, validation and serverless DMS are not modeled.
notInScope: Real source/target database engines outside the simulator

ec2.title: Amazon EC2 (instances, EBS, AMIs, load balancing, Auto Scaling)
ec2.summary: Vyomi implements the EC2 API in its own model (core/vpc_core.py and related cores); on the offline appliance each running instance is a Docker container with sshd, and in Nano it can optionally be a small Linux VM in the browser.
wire: boto3 / aws-cli / Terraform with only the endpoint changed

tech: Docker bridge networks + nftables (optional netsim enforcement)
offline.notes: The EC2 API state is in-house; RunInstances starts a real Docker container per instance (compute/backend.py, with LXD/Multipass as older runtimes). SSH, exec-based terminal, Instance Connect and per-container CPU/network/IO metrics are real; the container is a Linux userland, not an AMI.

tech: v86 x86 emulator + 21 MB Alpine image (opt-in)
nano.notes: Instance records always work. With in-browser VMs turned on (localStorage nano_vm_compute=1) each instance is a real 32-bit Alpine Linux VM in the tab with an xterm.js serial console; without it Connect returns NoRuntime. No Docker, no EC2 Instance Connect delivery, no instance metrics.

differs: Offline instances are Docker containers sharing the host kernel, not AMI-based virtual machines; AMIs are a curated list (Amazon Linux, Ubuntu, Debian, RHEL, SUSE, Windows) and Windows/RDP is not offered.
Nano VMs are 32-bit x86 Alpine, not the chosen AMI; RAM is the disk (Stop saves it, Terminate discards it); no general internet egress; a background tab runs several times slower.
A running instance passes status checks immediately; nothing becomes impaired on its own.
Key pairs are key-shaped documents; SSH uses the appliance's shared key pair, not the one chosen at launch.
Instance metadata does not vend IAM role credentials.
Snapshots complete instantly; Elastic IPs are synthetic addresses.
CPU, network and EBS metrics exist only offline (sampled from the container); Nano publishes none.

Spot never interrupts, Reserved Instances and Savings Plans have no billing effect, prices are illustrative, and on the offline appliance launch coupling for Spot, Capacity Reservations, Dedicated Hosts and scheduled events does not apply to the Docker runtime.
ELB target health is deterministic and no L7 traffic flows through load balancers.
Auto Scaling step scaling always applies the first step; warm pools and mixed-instances policies are not modeled.
notInScope: Real hypervisor (Nitro), GPU/Trainium, bare metal and UltraServers
Multi-AZ placement and real hardware faults
Real AMI Marketplace, billing and capacity markets
RDP/Windows guests, EBS volume durability and performance

elbv2.title: Elastic Load Balancing v2
elbv2.summary: Load balancer, listener and target group control plane in Vyomi's own core with no L7 data plane.

offline.notes: State in space-scoped state; target health derived from the EC2 instance state.

nano.notes: Same core in the tab.

differs: No traffic is balanced; target health is deterministic.
Attributes such as idle timeout are stored without behaviour; mutual TLS is never enforced.
notInScope: Real load balancer nodes, TLS termination and request metrics

autoscaling.title: EC2 Auto Scaling
autoscaling.summary: Group and policy engine in Vyomi's own core that launches and terminates instances through the EC2 model.

offline.notes: Scaling acts on the same instance model, so scaled instances become Docker containers offline.

nano.notes: Same core; instances are records (VMs only if in-browser VMs are on).

differs: Scheduled actions and instance refresh are evaluated lazily, not on a clock.
Step scaling applies its first step; target tracking nudges by one instance.
notInScope: Warm pools, mixed-instances policies, real capacity

dlm.title: Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager
dlm.summary: Snapshot/AMI lifecycle policies in Vyomi's own core, evaluated lazily.

offline.notes: Creates and prunes snapshots/AMIs through the EC2 model.

nano.notes: Same core.

differs: Only hourly Interval cadence is modeled; policies run when read, not on a live clock.
notInScope: Cross-account sharing and fast snapshot restore

imagebuilder.title: EC2 Image Builder
imagebuilder.summary: Image Builder API in Vyomi's own core; builds run for real only on the offline appliance through a container builder.

offline.notes: Recipe steps ExecuteBash, UpdateOS, Reboot and CreateFile are compiled to a Dockerfile and built from a base image already on the host.

nano.notes: Records only: every build ends FAILED with 'No container builder on this substrate'.

differs: Other actions (S3Download, WebDownload, PowerShell...) fail the build.
Pipeline schedules never fire; builds run synchronously.

mgn.title: AWS Application Migration Service
mgn.summary: Migration lifecycle in Vyomi's own core; no replication agent and no data is copied.

offline.notes: Test and cutover launch a real EC2 instance in the model from a synthetic AMI.

nano.notes: Same core.

differs: Source servers are registered with a Vyomi-only action; replication state advances on elapsed time.

instance-connect.title: EC2 Instance Connect
instance-connect.summary: SendSSHPublicKey validation in Vyomi's own core; key delivery works only offline.

offline.notes: Appends the key to the container user's authorized_keys for 60 seconds.

nano.notes: Validates the request but there is no guest to deliver the key to.

differs: Offline sessions use the appliance's shared key pair.

vpc.title: Amazon VPC and networking
vpc.summary: Vyomi models VPC resources in its own core and evaluates reachability with a shared network simulator (netsim); offline it can additionally enforce the rules on real packets with Docker bridges and nftables.
wire: boto3 / aws-cli / Terraform with only the endpoint changed

offline.notes: Enforcement is opt-in (VYOMI_NETSIM_ENFORCE=1|auto) and applies only to instances on the Docker compute backend; with it off the rules are only evaluated by Reachability Analyzer.

tech: Python VPC core + netsim evaluator in Pyodide
nano.notes: Control plane and logical evaluation only. No packets exist, so flow logs produce no records and NAT/IGW behaviour is evaluated, not enforced.

differs: Routes, security groups, NACLs, peering, NAT and transit gateway semantics are evaluated by netsim; packet enforcement exists only offline, only when enabled, and not for overlapping CIDRs across peered VPCs.
Elastic IP inbound DNAT is enforced only with VYOMI_NETSIM_INBOUND_DNAT=1.
Site-to-Site and Client VPN tunnels never come up and carry no packets; BGP routes are never learned.
Network Firewall, DNS Firewall, traffic mirroring, transit gateway policy tables and multicast are control-plane state with validation; no packets are inspected or mirrored.
NAT gateway metrics count evaluated connections, not real bytes.
Endpoints (PrivateLink) get ENIs and DNS names but do not proxy L7 traffic.
Only one Region (us-east-1) is modeled.
notInScope: Real data-plane throughput, Nitro networking and Direct Connect

lattice.title: Amazon VPC Lattice
lattice.summary: Control plane in Vyomi's own core plus an evaluated (not packet-level) data plane.

offline.notes: Service DNS, listener rules and auth policies are evaluated in Python.

nano.notes: Same evaluation in the tab.

differs: Requests are evaluated through a Vyomi invoke verb, not routed over a real network.

networkmanager.title: AWS Network Manager
networkmanager.summary: Inventory and registration control plane only.

offline.notes: Transit gateways are validated against the EC2 model.

nano.notes: Same core.

differs: No topology telemetry, events, route analysis, Connect or Direct Connect associations.

eks.title: Amazon EKS
eks.summary: On the offline appliance each EKS cluster is a real k3s Kubernetes control plane in Docker managed through Vyomi's EKS API; Nano has no Kubernetes.
wire: Kubernetes API (kubectl, kubeconfig from the k3s endpoint)

tech: k3s (Docker, one server container per cluster)
k3s agent containers as node group nodes
offline.notes: Requires Docker and VYOMI_K8S_BACKEND=k3s. Cluster status follows the server's /readyz; node groups are privileged k3s agent containers. Managed add-ons, Fargate and logging are recorded configuration, not deployed.

tech: EKS API core loads but no control plane
nano.notes: No Kubernetes control plane runs in the browser; managed Kubernetes is gated to the Pro/Max/Enterprise tiers (core/k8s_tier_gate.py). Registry level for Nano is not_simulated.

differs: k3s runs one pinned Kubernetes version whatever version is requested; the API reports the requested one.
The control-plane node is visible in kubectl get nodes and schedules workloads.
The endpoint is a published localhost port, not an eks.amazonaws.com host; the OIDC issuer discovery document is not served.
Cluster and node group updates are tracked records; the running k3s is not upgraded.
Networking uses flannel and storage uses local-path, not the VPC CNI or EBS CSI.
Access entries are stored; kubectl is gated by them only once the token webhook is wired in.
IRSA, Pod Identity, EKS Auto Mode and Hybrid Nodes are not simulated.
notInScope: Managed multi-AZ control plane and etcd
EC2 worker nodes, Fargate pod isolation

ecr.title: Amazon ECR
ecr.summary: Vyomi implements the ECR API and the Docker/OCI registry v2 wire in its own core, storing manifests and layers in the simulator's S3.
wire: Docker/OCI Registry HTTP API v2 (after aws ecr get-login-password)

offline.notes: Blobs are keyed by digest in bucket vyomi-ecr-<account>. A registry:2 container is present in the compose full profile but the ECR core stores blobs itself; whether the registry wire is proxied to it is not verified.

nano.notes: The registry wire is reachable only through the Nano relay or tunnel; a docker client cannot reach the browser tab directly, so use the ECR API (PutImage and layer upload) there.

differs: Layer tarballs are stored byte-for-byte and digest-verified but never unpacked or executed.
Scan findings come from a bundled advisory snapshot (a few dozen CVEs) or Trivy offline, not Amazon's feed.
Replication stays inside the simulator account; pull-through cache and cross-repository blob mount are not simulated.
GetDownloadUrlForLayer returns the registry blob URL, not a presigned S3 URL.
Lifecycle policies are evaluated on a tick or while the Nano page is open, not asynchronously within 24 hours.

lambda.title: AWS Lambda
lambda.summary: Vyomi implements the Lambda API in its own core and runs only Python handlers: in a separate Python process offline and in a restricted in-process sandbox in Nano.
wire: boto3 / aws-cli / SDKs with only the endpoint changed

offline.notes: Function code is written to lambda_functions/<name>/ and run in a subprocess with the function's environment, timeout and layers. No container or Firecracker is used.

nano.notes: Handler runs in a curated-builtins sandbox with a stdlib allow-list and no file, network or process access.

differs: Only Python executes; other runtimes can be selected and stored but Invoke still runs the source as Python.
Asynchronous invokes run immediately with a single attempt; there is no retry or backoff.
Layers are stored but not merged into the runtime; weighted alias routing is stored but not split.
Positive reserved concurrency is stored, not enforced (zero throttles).
SQS triggers fire synchronously; other event source types are stored without a poller unless wired through EventBridge, SNS or S3 notifications.
MicroVMs, capacity providers, network connectors and Lambda@Edge replicas are tracked records.
Code signing is enforced at deploy time only.
notInScope: Firecracker microVM isolation and cold starts
Node.js, Java, .NET, Go and container image functions executing

apigateway.title: Amazon API Gateway (REST, HTTP, WebSocket)
apigateway.summary: Vyomi implements API Gateway control and data planes in its own cores; Lambda proxy integrations call Vyomi's Lambda core.
wire: boto3 / aws-cli / Terraform with only the endpoint changed

tech: Caddy gateway (v2 execute-api listener, full profile)
offline.notes: The v2 data plane is handled in apigatewayv2_gateway.py behind the shared Caddy listener; REST (v1) invoke is exercised through Test Invoke. Whether v1 stages are served over a host-based listener is not verified.

tech: Python API Gateway cores in Pyodide
nano.notes: Control plane and in-core invoke (Test); real HTTP proxy and Lambda integrations run through the in-browser cores.

differs: AWS_IAM and Cognito authorizers are stored but not enforced on v1; only NONE is evaluated.
The execute-api invoke host is not resolvable from outside Vyomi; use Test or the appliance address.
Custom domains, client certificates and VPC links are stored; no ACM, Route 53 or NLB exists behind them.
WebSocket APIs have no connection registry or @connections management API.
Developer portals publish well-formed URLs that are not reachable.
notInScope: Real mTLS, WAF, usage metering and billing

states.title: AWS Step Functions
states.summary: Vyomi runs a real Amazon States Language interpreter in its own core, calling Vyomi's Lambda core for Task states.
wire: boto3 / aws-cli / SDKs with only the endpoint changed

offline.notes: State lives in the shared Step Functions store; Task states invoke the appliance's Lambda functions.

tech: Python Step Functions core in Pyodide
nano.notes: Same interpreter; Task states invoke the in-browser Lambda sandbox.

differs: Wait states complete instantly instead of sleeping.
Logging is delivered when an execution finishes, not while it runs.
X-Ray tracing produces traces in Vyomi's X-Ray core only.
notInScope: AWS-scale execution history retention and throughput

bedrock.title: Amazon Bedrock
bedrock.summary: Vyomi answers every Bedrock model call with one small local model (llama.cpp offline, WebLLM in the browser) behind Vyomi's own Bedrock, Agents, Knowledge Bases, Guardrails and AgentCore cores.
wire: boto3 / aws-cli / SDKs with only the endpoint changed

tech: llama.cpp llama-server container (vyomi-llm; SmolLM2-360M-Instruct GGUF by default)
feature-hash embeddings when no embedding model
offline.notes: The local model container is started explicitly (core/llm_runtime.py) and refuses to start below a free-disk guard. With no model running, calls fail with ModelNotReadyException; there is no canned fallback. Mesh appliances use a different, larger model setup (not verified here).

tech: WebLLM (@mlc-ai/web-llm, WebGPU, loaded from a CDN)
nano.notes: No model exists until the page enables the in-browser WebLLM model (needs WebGPU). The in-browser model serves the console page that loaded it, not the external SDK relay endpoint.

differs: Every model id (Claude, Nova, Titan, Llama, Mistral) is answered by the same small local model; quality is far below production models.
Images, documents, prompt caching and reasoning content are rejected with a validation error.
Knowledge bases ingest text files only and use exact cosine search; no managed vector store.
Agent action groups are stored but not invoked; AgentCore runtime runs a Vyomi agent spec, not your container.
Guardrails are deterministic word, topic and regex filters, not Bedrock's classifiers.
AgentCore gateway MCP endpoint is on the Vyomi wire path, not a *.gateway.bedrock-agentcore hostname.
notInScope: Foundation models themselves (Anthropic, Amazon, Meta, Mistral weights)
Provisioned throughput, model customization and evaluation jobs

cloudformation.title: AWS CloudFormation
cloudformation.summary: Vyomi implements CloudFormation in its own core and provisions only a fixed set of resource types through Vyomi's other service cores.
wire: boto3 / aws-cli / Terraform with only the endpoint changed

offline.notes: Stacks, change sets, stack sets and hooks live in space-scoped state; resources are created in the S3, DynamoDB, SNS, SQS, IAM and Logs cores.

nano.notes: Same core and the same resource set.

differs: Only AWS::S3::Bucket, DynamoDB::Table, SNS::Topic, SQS::Queue, IAM::Role, Logs::LogGroup and WaitCondition[Handle] are provisioned; a template with any other type fails and rolls back.
YAML support is a subset: multi-line short-form tag arguments are not supported.
Property-level drift is detected for a subset of properties; S3 buckets are existence-only.
StackSets record stack instances in the single account without creating real stacks in other accounts.
Hooks run one built-in check (required tags), not custom handler code.
Rollback triggers are evaluated once after the operation, with no monitoring window.
notInScope: EC2, VPC, Lambda, RDS and other resource types in templates

cloudwatch.title: Amazon CloudWatch and CloudWatch Logs
cloudwatch.summary: Vyomi implements metrics, alarms, dashboards and Logs in its own cores, with alarms evaluated on every PutMetricData.
wire: CloudWatch smithy-rpc-v2-cbor, JSON 1.0 and Query + XML
boto3 / aws-cli / SDKs with only the endpoint changed

offline.notes: Metrics, alarms and log events persist through the file-backed substrate; EC2, S3, DynamoDB, SQS and RDS publish real datapoints from their own activity.

tech: Python CloudWatch and Logs cores in Pyodide
nano.notes: Same engines; only metrics that Nano services actually generate exist (for example no EC2 CPU series).

differs: Alarm actions fire for SNS, Lambda, EC2 stop/terminate/reboot and Auto Scaling; EC2 Recover is not offered.
Anomaly detection is mean plus standard-deviation bands, not AWS's ML model.
Metrics Insights query supports a partial SQL subset; Logs Insights supports fields, filter, sort, limit, pattern and count stats only.
Live Tail polls FilterLogEvents instead of streaming.
Log transformers run four processors; data protection recognizes 8 managed identifiers.
Automatic dashboards exist only for services with real metric integrations (currently EC2).
notInScope: Synthetics canaries, RUM and Application Signals

cost-explorer.title: AWS Cost Explorer
cost-explorer.summary: Vyomi computes what AWS would have charged from the simulator's own EC2, EBS and RDS inventory and uptime, using illustrative on-demand list prices.

offline.notes: Accrues hourly rates by real uptime of simulated resources.

nano.notes: Same engine over the browser stores.

differs: Only EC2, EBS and RDS are metered; other services show no cost.
Prices are illustrative on-demand rates; nothing is billed.
Hourly granularity, tag and cost-category grouping, and ML forecasting are not modeled; forecasts extrapolate the current run rate.
Stopped instances accrue nothing from when they are observed stopped.
notInScope: Real billing data, invoices, credits, Savings Plans amortization

eventbridge.title: Amazon EventBridge
eventbridge.summary: Vyomi implements event buses, rules, archives, Scheduler, Pipes and Schemas in its own cores on the same messaging store as SQS and SNS, so routed events are real deliveries.
wire: boto3 / aws-cli / Terraform with only the endpoint changed

tech: Vyomi EventBridge, Scheduler and Schemas cores (Python)
offline.notes: Targets SQS, SNS, Lambda, Step Functions and Kinesis are actually invoked. API destinations send real HTTP requests.

nano.notes: Same engines; Lambda targets run in the in-browser sandbox.

differs: Other target types (ECS, Batch, CodeBuild, API destinations on Nano...) are accepted and stored without being invoked, except API destinations offline.
Archives keep the bus's latest 500 events in a bounded log; replay is synchronous within that window.
Schedules fire the next time any Scheduler API call occurs after their due time, not on a clock.
Only SQS is a delivering Pipes source; filtering, enrichment and input templates are stored, not applied.
Global endpoints do no failover; partner event sources act within one account.
OAuth client-credentials for API destinations is not performed.
notInScope: SaaS partner integrations at the source

kinesis.title: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams
kinesis.summary: Vyomi implements Kinesis Data Streams in its own core with real shard hashing, sequence numbers, iterators and split/merge.
wire: boto3 / aws-cli / SDKs with only the endpoint changed

offline.notes: Streams and record logs persist in the space-scoped state; routes/aws_kinesis.py serves the wire.

nano.notes: Same core in the tab.

differs: Resource policies are stored and returned but never evaluated.
Other differences from AWS (throughput limits, enhanced fan-out) are not listed in the registry and were not verified.
notInScope: KCL lease tables beyond what DynamoDB provides

malware-protection.title: GuardDuty Malware Protection for S3
malware-protection.summary: Vyomi scans new S3 uploads with its own hash and literal-signature scanner, not an antivirus engine.

offline.notes: Runs synchronously on upload, including zip members to two levels; raises an Object:S3/MaliciousFile finding.

nano.notes: Same scanner in the tab.

differs: Detects the EICAR and Vyomi test strings plus signatures the operator registers; no heuristics, behavioural analysis or vendor threat intelligence.
Covers only new uploads; objects over 64 MiB are reported unsupported.
No EventBridge scan-result events.
notInScope: Real antivirus engines and threat intelligence

panels.title: AWS Network Manager
panels.summary: Vyomi models Network Manager inventory and transit gateway registration in its own core, with no telemetry.

offline.notes: Global networks, sites, devices, links and registrations persist in state; a registered transit gateway must exist in the EC2/VPC model.

nano.notes: Same core.

differs: No topology telemetry, events, route analysis, Connect attachments or Direct Connect/customer-gateway associations.
notInScope: Real SD-WAN devices and live network telemetry

redshift.title: Amazon Redshift
redshift.summary: Vyomi implements the Redshift cluster API and Redshift Data API in its own core, running SQL on an in-memory SQLite engine.
wire: boto3 / aws-cli with only the endpoint changed

tech: sqlite3 (in memory, statement log replayed after restart)
offline.notes: State lives on the RDS store; writes are kept as a statement log and replayed when the engine is rebuilt.

nano.notes: Same core and engine in the tab.

differs: The SQL dialect is SQLite's: no distkey/sortkey, columnar storage, COPY/UNLOAD, Spectrum or stored procedures.
Node types and counts are metadata; no snapshots, resize or WLM.
The database is single-schema; public is accepted and ignored.
There is no Redshift console page yet; use the CLI or SDK.

securityhub.title: AWS Security Hub and GuardDuty
securityhub.summary: Vyomi derives findings from the simulator's own resources and audit feed with deterministic rules, not from AWS threat intelligence.

offline.notes: Posture rules run over stored resources; threat detection runs over the control-plane calls the appliance served.

nano.notes: Same rules over browser stores.

differs: Security Hub implements a small subset of Foundational Security Best Practices controls (S3.2, S3.4, S3.8, EC2.9, EC2.13, EC2.14, RDS.2, RDS.3, IAM.5, CloudTrail.1); no CIS or PCI standards and no cross-Region aggregation.
GuardDuty findings carry detector=vyomi-rules; there is no network flow, DNS or CloudTrail stream and no machine-learning detection.
CreateSampleFindings creates findings labelled [SAMPLE].
notInScope: GuardDuty ML anomaly detection, runtime monitoring, EBS malware scanning, S3/EKS/RDS protection plans

ssm.title: AWS Systems Manager
ssm.summary: Vyomi implements Parameter Store, Documents, Run Command, State Manager, Maintenance Windows, Patch Baselines and Session Manager in its own core without an SSM Agent fleet.
wire: boto3 / aws-cli / SDKs with only the endpoint changed

offline.notes: SecureString values are encrypted at rest with the KMS core. Running Docker instances register as managed nodes and Session Manager runs a command-at-a-time shell in the container.

tech: v86 VM shell (only when in-browser VMs are on)
nano.notes: Parameter Store and documents work. Sessions work only from the console page against a running in-browser VM; the SDK/CLI relay answers TargetNotConnected.

differs: Run Command completes immediately as Success with no real command output.
State Manager associations never advance past Pending/Creating.
Patch baselines are stored and never evaluated against instance patch state.
The ssmmessages data channel is not served, so the AWS CLI session-manager-plugin cannot attach; use the console session or ssh.
